species.name: Lake trout
why: Water 46°F on top, a bit cool for them, so they feed in the warmest water they can find.
Best water today is 26–120 ft deep, mostly on open water over the deep basin.
The lake is layered: warm water down to about 105 ft, cold below.

species.name: Yellow perch
why: Water 46°F on top, much colder than they like, so they move slowly and stay deep.
Best water today is 8–38 ft deep, mostly on channel edges.
The lake is layered: warm water down to about 105 ft, cold below.

species.name: Northern pike
why: Water 46°F on top, much colder than they like, so they move slowly and stay deep.
Best water today is 2–20 ft deep, mostly on channel edges.
The lake is layered: warm water down to about 105 ft, cold below.
Southwest wind at 8 mph pushes bait onto the northeast shore: try the wind-blown banks.
